summary: Established a coding-agent utility gate and a dated append-only audit trail for canonical knowledge changes.
rationale: Paper-level ingestion can add redundant or weakly actionable material that reduces retrieval precision and raises maintenance cost.
practical_impact: Future promotions must be novel, decision-relevant, actionable or testable, evidence-bounded, and accompanied by a dated change record.

summary: Added a narrow navigable-source tool and regression-test contract to the existing iterative retrieval pattern.
rationale: Stable source-local positions, explicit seen-result handling and separated mutation authority close an operational gap without duplicating established agentic RAG patterns or promoting vendor benchmarks.
practical_impact: Document-research and coding agents can now be tested for anchor-preserving navigation, repeat-result termination, tenant isolation and read-only retrieval authority.

summary: Improved coding-agent discoverability with a dedicated knowledge lane, technique-card cross-links, AGENTS.md consumption contract, retrieval eval cases, and a compile-generated technique index.
rationale: Coding-agent content was searchable but weakly connected through lanes, pattern-to-card links, and retrieval regression coverage compared with RAG and security topics.
practical_impact: Coding agents can now enter through a curated lane, resolve technique_id paths deterministically, and be regression-tested for harness, instruction, skill, and replay queries.

summary: Restricted the relaxed search fallback to selective terms and added a calibrated match confidence signal plus a read-first navigation and scope contract for agents.
rationale: The previous OR fallback matched filler tokens, so out-of-scope questions returned confident-looking noise with no signal that the topic is uncovered.
practical_impact: Out-of-scope queries now report low or none confidence with an advisory, the coverage floor is calibrated against the labelled retrieval pack, and agents are directed to navigate and load canonical sections before searching.

summary: Separated the human entry point in README.md from toolchain and governance internals, moving the latter into a new docs/contributing.md, and corrected a stale description of the search fallback in docs/architecture.md.
rationale: README.md had grown to duplicate setup and search instructions and led with internal governance rules instead of what the knowledge base covers, while its search description no longer matched the selective-term fallback and confidence signal already shipped.
practical_impact: README.md is now a short human-first overview that still preserves the setup, quality-check, and public-API pointers relied on by AGENTS.md and the generated index.md; repository layout, the promotion gate, and the full command reference now live in docs/contributing.md; and docs/architecture.md documents the actual retrieval fallback and confidence behavior.

summary: Added a required technique-card lifecycle with an audited retirement gate, and defaulted search to reviewed and contested pages so immature or retired material no longer answers questions.
rationale: The retirement machinery existed for pages and claims but had never been used, and did not exist at all for technique cards, so all 132 cards presented as equally current and the catalogue could only grow. Search additionally applied no status filter by default, admitting inbox and draft sections into results.
practical_impact: Every card now declares recommended, situational, legacy or deprecated. Legacy and deprecated cards require a retirement reason and an applied supersession record in the change ledger, which an ordinary technique record does not satisfy, and lint rejects successors that are unknown, self-referential, retired or cyclic, plus live cards that carry retirement metadata. technique-index.json publishes lifecycle and successors on the exact-lookup path. Search omits inbox, draft, superseded and archived unless --any-status is passed and reports status_filter_source. All existing cards were seeded as situational, so recommended is scarce and must be granted alongside the routing page that names the family default.

summary: Promoted nine routing-default technique cards to recommended and updated the parser, chunking, retrieval and coding-agent catalog pages to name them explicitly.
rationale: Every card had been seeded situational, so agents had no deterministic default despite routing pages already naming PyMuPDF, Docling, recursive splitting, BM25, dense retrieval and the three coding-agent harness cards as first choices.
practical_impact: technique-index.json now exposes nine recommended defaults; agents should propose these first and escalate only when use_when or routing conditions say otherwise. Retrieval eval cases for parser and chunking defaults were added and verified.

summary: Retired fixed token windows to legacy as an ablation-only control and named recursive boundary-aware splitting as the production baseline.
rationale: The chunking routing defaults already treat recursive splitting as the cheap production baseline and fixed windows as a reproducible control; leaving both situational let agents treat them as equally recommendable.
practical_impact: chunking.fixed.token-window is legacy with superseded_by chunking.fixed.recursive-split; the chunking catalog now states fixed windows are ablation-only. Retrieval eval cases for the chunking default were checked and still pass.
